rationale: drop3 is a 3-function, ~1.1KB bit-manipulation benchmark whose core (drop_0xx) runs in a tight data-processing loop, so the table favors low-overhead arithmetic and structural passes while penalizing branch-heavy transformations: SUB gets the highest security/diversity weights because instruction substitution obscures the bitwise drop logic cheaply and with near-zero correctness risk; SPLIT is weighted as a cheap enabler that improves FLA's effectiveness on the two substantial function bodies (drop_0xx, main) without measurable cost; FLA is moderately favored for its strong control-flow hiding on these small functions but with elevated RuntimeCost weight to keep the dispatch loop out of drop_0xx's hot path if features indicate it; BCF is retained with a lower security weight and very high RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights since bogus predicates both bloat a 1KB text segment and tax the hot loop disproportionately; IBR is kept at low security weight with high runtime/correctness-risk weights because indirect branching adds dispatch overhead and fragility for little gain on so few basic blocks; ICALL and IGV are omitted entirely — with three functions, no meaningful indirect-call sites or global-variable surface, indirection there buys diversity only on paper while directly degrading the timed loop and _start.
